title: observability: token-level cost/latency breakdowns, kv-cache metrics, dashboards + alert tuning
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: ops and platform teams need better token-level visibility to accurately attribute cost and latency regressions to model variants, routing policies, and KV-cache effectiveness. This PR adds token-level cost/latency breakdowns, KV cache hit/miss metrics exposed in Prometheus, extended tracing spans for per-token latency, updated Grafana dashboards, and tuned alerts to reduce noisy paging while still catching regressions. Changes include metric name conventions, a small semantic change to the runtime request lifecycle to emit per-token timing, schema updates for dashboard panels, and a runbook section. Checklist: - [x] Add Prometheus metrics (token_cost_us, token_latency_us, token_kv_cache_hit) - [x] Wire tracing spans to include token_index and kv_cache_hit tags - [x] Update grafana dashboards and dashboard JSON definitions - [x] Tune alert thresholds and add a suppression policy for canaries - [x] Update observability docs and runbook - [x] Add unit + integration tests for metrics emission Notes: Kept metric cardinality low by limiting token histogram buckets and adding label normalizations for model_family and route. This description contains the full context and rationale in a single continuous string.

Aisha Kumar (2025-02-20): Addressed: lowered p99 to 1.5s, added canary suppression policy in prometheus rules and an annotation explaining rationale.
